title: Anki & Spaced Repetition System (SRS) Optimization Guide
evaluation: ⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐ (5/5) — Most Scientifically Validated Method for Long-Term Memory

sm2_vs_fsrs.sm2: Standard SuperMemo-2 algorithm from 1987. Uses a fixed Ease Factor that can lead to 'Ease Hell' when cards are graded 'Hard'.
sm2_vs_fsrs.fsrs: Free Spaced Repetition Scheduler (2023+). Uses DSR model (Difficulty, Stability, Retrievability) based on modern cognitive psychology. Reduces total review burden by 20–30% while maintaining target retention (e.g. 90%).

the_20_rules_of_formulating_knowledge_su: Rule 1: Do not learn if you do not understand (Comprehension precedes memorization).
Rule 2: Learn before you memorize (Build the mental model first).
Rule 3: Build upon the basics (Establish foundational vocabulary before niche idioms).
Rule 4: Stick to the Minimum Information Principle (Each flashcard must test exactly ONE atomic fact).
Rule 5: Cloze deletion is easy and effective (Sentence context prevents ambiguous recall).
Rule 6: Use imagery and emotional cues.
Rule 7: Avoid sets and enumerations (Break lists of 5 items into 5 distinct cards).

minimal_pairs_phonetics_tsv.front: Minimal pair: /iː/ vs /ɪ/ -> Did you say *leave* or *live*?
minimal_pairs_phonetics_tsv.back: leave = /liːv/ (Tense, closing diphthong) | live = /lɪv/ (Lax, short near-front)

minimal_pairs_phonetics_tsv.front: Minimal pair: /æ/ vs /e/ -> Did you say *bad* or *bed*?
minimal_pairs_phonetics_tsv.back: bad = /bæd/ (Open front, jaw drops) | bed = /bed/ (Mid front, narrower jaw)

minimal_pairs_phonetics_tsv.front: Minimal pair: /θ/ vs /t/ -> Did you say *three* or *tree*?
minimal_pairs_phonetics_tsv.back: three = /θriː/ (Tongue between teeth, friction) | tree = /triː/ (Tongue on alveolar ridge, plosive)
